method.prd_rate: Assumes Automata finish at the rate of the last three active days.
method.task_rate: Assumes tasks finish at the average rate over all active days so far.
method.task_rate_24h: Assumes tasks finish at the rate of the last 24 hours of active time.
method.worker_hours: Assumes each task takes the average worker time of a completed task and workers stay as busy as they have been per active day.

unfiled_rows.item: BL556 Parallel tasks inside one PRD: DAGs allow it (46 PRDs since 10-19: 5.5 tasks, critical path 3.2, so up to 1.7x faster) but `autonomous.max_concurrent_tasks` is 1 and the project-tree write lock (BL428 Phase 2) serializes writers on one worktree. Needs per-task isolated worktrees plus a merge step, or write-dir partitioning. Design first.

unfiled_rows.item: BL483 Automation policy: every option for how automation runs is configurable per project (release rules, cadence, lane limits, backends and models, retry and escalation limits, plan checks, override-lock states, git default, timeouts, defect intake, escalation channel, minimum model context 64k, pinned model per node and the model-swap rule), with our tested behaviour as the shipped default policy ([model host requirements](2026-10-18-model-host-requirements.md)); belongs inside BL431 Phase 2 and BL473

Upstream monitoring (operator 2026-10-25: "consume patches when available ... future project monitoring all upstream"): watch every upstream dependency, base image and advisory feed and open the upgrade the moment a security patch is published, replacing the 72-hour waiting rule withdrawn on 2026-10-25. Until it exists the supervisor and the release path consume security patches as they find them. Needs design (sources, cadence, which updates are auto-merged, how malicious-release risk is handled now that the waiting period is gone)
